71: $99 a room is where stretching starts here. Ripples in a rambler usually turn up first in the hallway, where every trip through the house lands, and a power stretcher pulls that slack out again at roughly a fifth the price of new carpet. As long as the pile bounces back and the color still works, stretch it.
79: Four things push a floor past saving: traffic lanes crushed flat, seams letting go, backing that crumbles when you touch it, or pet smell that outlasted a professional cleaning. Short of those, a power stretch at $99 per room is the cheaper answer — and the bedrooms of a Shoreline split-entry, mostly under furniture, usually qualify. Pile that springs back and a color you still like are the test. We look before anything gets quoted.
83: Start with the pad rather than the carpet: a moisture barrier is what keeps an accident from soaking into the subfloor of a fifties rambler, and a soaked subfloor is where odor becomes permanent. Above it, solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing — fiber that takes diluted bleach without fading. Budget $0.65 per square foot for the barrier pad. It rides along on the visit, so you can press a thumb into it before deciding.
85: Read the mill's fine print before you settle on a pad: plenty of mills set a minimum pad grade as a condition of coverage, which is one reason all three grades ride along on the visit. That carpet warranty covers wear and stains for 10 to 25 years, scaled to grade. Underneath it sits OC Flooring's 1-year workmanship warranty, which covers the basement stairs and seams too. Your written quote states both.
